nonTeachingWeeks.what: Routines, read-aloud habits, discussion rules, and the beginning-of-year screening: letter names, letter sounds, rhyming, first-sound fluency.
End of the first quarter: report-card checks and family conferences.
The short week before winter break: review stations and favorite read-alouds, no new lesson.
Middle-of-year benchmark window: letter-sound fluency, phoneme segmentation, first nonsense words.
End of the third quarter: report-card checks and spring conferences.
End-of-year benchmark window.
Last week of school: review stations, class book share, and summer reading packets.

units.title: Letters and Handwriting
units.why: Letter names and letter formation come first in Kindergarten: every later sound, word, and sentence lesson needs them.

units.title: How Books and Print Work
units.why: Once children know letters, they learn how print carries the words they hear: the book, the direction, the word, and the space.

lessons.title: Front cover, back cover, and title page
lessons.objective: Children find and name the front cover, the back cover, and the title page of a book and show where the story starts.
lessons.page: Print-concepts mini-book: one sheet that folds into an 8-page book with a front cover, a title page, six pages of one short sentence each, and a back cover. The child colors the front cover, circles the title on the title page, puts a star on the back cover, and numbers the pages. Level 1: the parts carry picture labels; level 2: the child matches the words cover, title, page to the parts; level 3: the child writes the title on the cover and on the title page.

lessons.title: Read left to right, top to bottom
lessons.objective: Children follow printed words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page while the teacher reads, pointing to each word.
lessons.page: Print-concepts page: three big-print sentences of 4 to 6 words that run over two lines, each with a green start dot and a red stop dot. The child traces the arrow along each line and the return-sweep arrow down to the next line, then touches each word while the teacher reads. Level 1: arrows printed, the child traces them; level 2: the child draws the arrows; level 3: the child numbers the words in reading order.

lessons.title: One spoken word, one written word
lessons.objective: Children match each word they say in a short sentence to one written word on the page, pointing word by word.
lessons.page: Print-concepts page: six pictures, each with a short sentence (I see a cat.) and a row of empty boxes under it, one box per word. The child says the sentence, points to each word, and colors one box per word. Level 1: 3-word sentences; level 2: 4- and 5-word sentences; level 3: the child matches each spoken sentence to the printed one of the same length.

lessons.title: Spaces between words: count the words
lessons.objective: Children find the spaces that separate printed words, count the words in a sentence, and leave a finger space when they copy one.
lessons.page: Print-concepts page: five sentences in big print with clear spaces; the child draws a line in each space, counts the words, and writes the number. Bottom: the child copies one sentence and leaves a finger space between the words. Level 1: 3-word sentences with dotted spaces; level 2: 4- and 5-word sentences; level 3: 5- and 6-word sentences and the copy task.

units.title: Hearing Sounds in Words
units.why: Phonemic awareness grows in a set order (rhyme, syllables, onset and rime, single sounds) and is the ground for reading the first words.

lessons.title: Blend the first sound and the rest
lessons.objective: Children blend a spoken first sound and the rest of a one-syllable word (/m/ + /op/) into the whole word and find its picture.
lessons.page: Sound-play picture page: eight rows of three pictures; the teacher says a word in two parts (/s/ ... /un/) and the child circles the picture of the whole word. Bottom: the child splits two picture words aloud into first sound and rest for a partner. Level 1: the three pictures start with different sounds; level 2: same first sound, different rest (sun, sock, sad); level 3: same rest, different first sound (cat, hat, bat).

units.title: First Words to Read
units.why: With letter sounds and blending started, the class reads its first words: pictures and words, heart words, and a first patterned book.

lessons.title: Read a little book with a pattern
lessons.objective: Children read a short picture book with a repeating sentence (I see a ...), using the heart words and the picture to read the new word on each page.

units.title: Short Vowels and CVC Words
units.why: In winter letters and sounds come together: the class reads and spells CVC words vowel by vowel, meets its first two-letter sounds, and reads a decodable book.

lessons.title: Vowels and consonants
lessons.objective: Children sort letters into vowels and consonants and find the vowel in short words they can read.

lessons.title: Short a and short i
lessons.objective: Children say the short sounds of a and i and read and spell CVC words with them, such as cat, map, pig, and sit.
lessons.page: Phonics pattern page: twelve picture words with the target spelling. Top: the child reads each word and draws a line to its picture. Bottom: the child writes the missing letters (c_t, p_g). Level 1: one pattern per page (short a); level 2: two patterns mixed (short a and short i), sorted into two columns; level 3: the whole word written under each picture.

lessons.title: Short o, short u, and short e
lessons.objective: Children say the short sounds of o, u, and e and read and spell CVC words with them, such as hot, bug, and bed.
lessons.page: Phonics pattern page: twelve picture words with the target spelling. Top: the child reads each word and draws a line to its picture. Bottom: the child writes the missing letters (h_t, b_g, b_d). Level 1: one pattern per page (short o); level 2: two patterns mixed, sorted into two columns; level 3: all three vowels, with the whole word written under each picture.

lessons.title: Change one sound to make a new word
lessons.objective: Children change the first, last, or middle sound of a spoken CVC word to make a new word (cat to hat, hat to ham, ham to him) and spell each new word.
lessons.page: Phonics chain page: a word ladder of six CVC words with pictures; each rung changes one letter. The child reads the top word, listens to the change the teacher says, and writes the new word on the next rung. Level 1: only the first sound changes; level 2: the first or the last sound; level 3: the first, last, or middle sound.

lessons.title: Which word matches: cat or cot?
lessons.objective: Children tell apart two words that differ by one letter (cat and cot, pin and pen) by saying the sound of the letter that differs and choosing the word for the picture.
lessons.page: Phonics pattern page: ten pictures, each with two words that differ by one letter (bag and big, hen and pen). The child reads both words, circles the word for the picture, and underlines the letter that differs. Level 1: the different letter is the first one; level 2: the last one; level 3: the middle vowel.

lessons.title: Read a decodable book
lessons.objective: Children read a short book made only of CVC words they can sound out and taught heart words, page by page, and draw what each page says.

units.title: Reading Stories
units.why: After a fall of read-alouds, the class learns the questions a reader asks of any story: who, where, what happened, and what the pictures add.

lessons.title: Who is in the story, and where?
lessons.objective: Children name the characters and the setting of a story read aloud and tell one major event, pointing to the pictures that show them.
lessons.page: Story and questions page: a read-aloud story of 4 to 6 picture panels with about 60 words that the teacher reads. Below: three boxes, Who? Where? What happened?, where the child answers. Level 1: the child circles the character and the place from three pictures each; level 2: the child draws them; level 3: the child draws and writes a label for each box.

lessons.title: Retell the story: beginning, middle, end
lessons.objective: Children retell a familiar story with its beginning, middle, and end, using the key details and the pictures.
lessons.page: Story and questions page: a read-aloud story of 4 to 6 picture panels with about 60 words that the teacher reads. Below: three boxes labeled beginning, middle, end. Level 1: the child cuts out three pictures and glues them in order; level 2: the child draws each part; level 3: the child draws each part and finishes a frame (First ___. Then ___. At the end ___.).

lessons.title: Ask and answer questions about a story
lessons.objective: Children answer who, what, where, and why questions about key details in a story read aloud and ask one question of their own.
lessons.page: Story and questions page: a read-aloud story of 4 to 6 picture panels with about 60 words and four questions the teacher reads (Who lost the hat? Where did it go?); the child circles the picture answer from three. Level 1: who and where questions; level 2: what and why questions; level 3: the child also draws or dictates a question of their own in a question-mark box.

lessons.title: The pictures and the words
lessons.objective: Children tell which moment in a story a picture shows and match each picture to the sentence it goes with.
lessons.page: Story and questions page: six sentences and six pictures from one short story in mixed order; the teacher reads each sentence and the child draws a line to its picture. Level 1: three sentences; level 2: six sentences; level 3: one sentence has no picture, and the child draws it.

lessons.title: Two stories, two adventures
lessons.objective: Children compare the adventures of two characters in two familiar stories and tell one thing that is the same and one that is different.
lessons.page: Two-text comparison page: two short read-aloud texts with picture panels side by side (a lost puppy, a lost kitten). Below: a two-circle diagram with a shared middle. Level 1: the child sorts six picture cards into the two circles and the middle; level 2: the child draws one thing that is the same and one that is different; level 3: the child draws and labels them.

units.title: Words and Sentences
units.why: With first words read, the class turns to the sentence: naming and action words, place words, the capital at the start, and the mark at the end.

lessons.title: Naming words and action words
lessons.objective: Children sort pictured words into naming words (dog, cup) and action words (run, jump) and say each in a sentence.
lessons.page: Grammar page: twelve picture words, half things and half actions, to cut and sort into a naming box and an action box. Level 1: pictures only; level 2: pictures with the word under each; level 3: the child also writes one naming word and one action word into a sentence frame (The ___ can ___.).

lessons.title: In, on, under, next to
lessons.objective: Children use the place words in, on, under, next to, behind, and in front of to tell where a thing is in a picture.
lessons.page: Grammar page: six scenes, each with a cat in, on, under, next to, behind, or in front of a box; the child circles the place word for each scene. Level 1: in, on, under; level 2: all six words; level 3: the child draws the cat where a printed sentence tells (The cat is under the bed.).

lessons.title: A sentence starts with a capital letter
lessons.objective: Children find the capital letter at the start of a sentence and in the word I, and fix sentences that start with a small letter.
lessons.page: Grammar page: six short sentences in big print; the child circles the first letter and every word I. Three of them start with a small letter, and the child writes the capital above it. Level 1: 3-word sentences; level 2: 4- and 5-word sentences; level 3: the child also copies one fixed sentence.

lessons.title: A period or a question mark?
lessons.objective: Children name the period and the question mark, tell which one ends a telling sentence and which one ends an asking sentence, and add the right mark.
lessons.page: Grammar page: eight sentences without end marks, half telling and half asking, each with a picture; the child writes a period or a question mark. Level 1: the teacher reads every sentence; level 2: the child reads with picture support; level 3: the child also writes one telling and one asking sentence about a picture.

lessons.title: Say more: make the sentence longer
lessons.objective: Children say and write a complete sentence about a picture and make it longer by adding where, when, or how (The dog runs to the park.).
lessons.page: Grammar page: four pictures, each with a short sentence (The dog runs.) and a box of add-ons (fast, to the park, in the rain). The child reads the sentence, picks an add-on that fits the picture, and writes the longer sentence. Level 1: the child circles the add-on; level 2: the child copies the longer sentence; level 3: the child writes an add-on of their own.

units.title: Sorting Words and Word Meanings
units.why: In spring vocabulary deepens: sorting by category, odd one out, opposites, words with two meanings, and verbs that show how an action is done.

lessons.title: Words with two meanings
lessons.objective: Children find the two meanings of a known word (a bat that flies, a bat for baseball) and choose the meaning that fits a sentence.
lessons.page: Word meaning page: six words with two meanings (bat, duck, ring, bark, top, can), each shown with two pictures. The teacher reads a sentence with the word and the child circles the picture that fits it. Level 1: three words; level 2: six words; level 3: the child draws the other meaning and says a sentence for it.

lessons.title: Walk, march, tiptoe: act it out
lessons.objective: Children act out verbs with close meanings (walk, march, tiptoe, stomp, prance) and tell how one action is different from the other.
lessons.page: Routine: the teacher shows a picture card and says one verb (walk, march, tiptoe, stomp); the class acts it out in place. Then two children act two verbs side by side and the class tells the difference (quiet or loud, slow or fast). Second day: toss, throw, fling and nibble, munch, gobble. Listen for: children choosing the exact verb when they describe a classmate's action.

units.title: Reading to Learn: Fact Texts
units.why: In spring the class reads to learn about the world: questions, the main topic, the pictures, how two ideas connect, and two texts on one topic.

lessons.title: Ask and answer questions about a fact text
lessons.objective: Children answer who, what, where, and how questions about key details in a short information text read aloud and ask a question of their own.
lessons.page: Fact text and questions page: an information text of four sentences in big print (about 30 words) about one animal or thing, with a photo-style picture. Below: four questions the teacher reads; the child circles the picture answer. Level 1: answers from three pictures; level 2: the child draws the answer; level 3: the child also draws a fact and dictates or writes a question about the topic.

lessons.title: What is it all about? The main topic
lessons.objective: Children name the main topic of a short information text and retell two key details about it.
lessons.page: Fact text and questions page: an information text of four sentences in big print (about 30 words) with one picture. Below: a topic box (circle one of three pictures) and two key-detail boxes. Level 1: the child circles the topic and one detail; level 2: the child draws two details; level 3: the child draws and labels two details.

lessons.title: Pictures that teach
lessons.objective: Children tell what a labeled picture in a fact text shows and match each sentence to the part of the picture it explains.
lessons.page: Fact text and questions page: an information text of four sentences about a plant with a labeled picture (roots, stem, leaf, flower). The child draws a line from each sentence to the part of the picture it tells about. Level 1: two labels; level 2: four labels; level 3: the child adds a label to a part that has none.

lessons.title: First this, then that: connect two ideas
lessons.objective: Children tell how two events or ideas in an information text connect, such as an egg and a chick, or rain and a puddle.
lessons.page: Fact text and questions page: an information text of four sentences about a change (an egg hatches into a chick). Below: two boxes joined by an arrow; the child shows the first and the second thing. Level 1: the child cuts and glues two pictures in order; level 2: the child draws both; level 3: the child draws both and finishes a frame (First ___, then ___.).

lessons.title: Two texts, one topic
lessons.objective: Children find what is the same and what is different in two short information texts about the same topic.
lessons.page: Two-text comparison page: two short read-aloud texts side by side on one topic (two kinds of bears, three sentences each, each with a picture). Below: a two-circle diagram with a shared middle. Level 1: the child sorts six picture cards into the two circles and the middle; level 2: the child draws one thing that is the same and one that is different; level 3: the child draws and labels them.

units.title: Draw and Write: Opinions, Facts, and Stories
units.why: By spring children sound out and spell CVC words and some heart words, so they write the three kinds of text with a picture and sentence frames.

lessons.title: My favorite and why: an opinion
lessons.objective: Children draw and write their opinion about a book or a topic (My favorite is ... I like it because ...) after the class votes.
lessons.page: Writing page (opinion): a box for a picture and three writing lines with the frames My favorite ___ is ___. I like it because ___. At the bottom, a checklist of three picture icons: I drew it. I wrote my opinion. I told why. Level 1: the child copies one word into each frame from a word bank; level 2: the child fills the frames with sounded-out words; level 3: open lines with a starter word only.

lessons.title: Teach a fact: draw, label, and write
lessons.objective: Children draw a topic they know, label its parts, and write one or two facts about it.
lessons.page: Writing page (informative): a box for a labeled drawing and three writing lines with the frames This is a ___. It has ___. It can ___. At the bottom, a checklist of three picture icons: I named my topic. I labeled my picture. I wrote a fact. Level 1: the child copies one word into each frame from a word bank; level 2: the child fills the frames with sounded-out words; level 3: open lines with a starter word only.

lessons.title: What happened to me: a small moment
lessons.objective: Children draw and write about one event in the order it happened and tell how they felt about it.
lessons.page: Writing page (narrative): two boxes for pictures (first, then) and three writing lines with the frames First I ___. Then I ___. I felt ___. At the bottom, a checklist of three picture icons: I drew two parts. I wrote what happened. I told how I felt. Level 1: the child copies one word into each frame from a word bank; level 2: the child fills the frames with sounded-out words; level 3: open lines with a starter word only.

lessons.title: Author's chair: a friend asks, I add
lessons.objective: Children read their writing to the class, answer a classmate's question about it, and add one detail to the picture or the words.
lessons.page: Routine: three children a day sit in the author's chair and read a writing page from this unit. The teacher pulls a name stick; that child asks one question (Where were you? What color was it?). The author adds the answer to the picture or the sentence with a colored pencil. Listen for: questions that ask for a detail, and an author who adds it.

leftOut.what: A or an? (K:articles)
leftOut.why: Choosing a or an is Grade 1 grammar (L.1.1.h) and is taught there in 'A or an: sort the words'; in Kindergarten children use a and an correctly in speech without a page.

leftOut.what: RL.K.4 and RI.K.4: ask about unknown words in a text
leftOut.why: A daily read-aloud routine (stop, ask, explain the word), not a separate lesson.

leftOut.what: RL.K.5: recognize storybooks and poems
leftOut.why: Taught in the daily read-aloud and the poem of the week, where the class names the kind of text each time.

leftOut.what: RL.K.6 and RI.K.6: name the author and the illustrator
leftOut.why: Part of introducing every read-aloud book (cover, author, illustrator); the cover-and-title-page lesson starts it.

leftOut.what: RL.K.10 and RI.K.10: group reading activities with purpose
leftOut.why: This is the daily read-aloud and shared reading itself, a routine every day of the year.

leftOut.what: RI.K.8: the reasons an author gives
leftOut.why: Kindergarten fact texts of four sentences hardly give reasons; met with prompting in the read-aloud of opinion picture books, not on a page.

leftOut.what: W.K.6: digital tools to publish writing
leftOut.why: Needs devices and adult help at a screen; it cannot be taught on a printed page or with a projector tool.

leftOut.what: W.K.7: shared research and writing projects
leftOut.why: A class book built over several weeks in science and read-aloud time, not a two-day lesson; the fact-text unit and the informative writing lesson prepare it.

leftOut.what: W.K.8: recall information from experiences
leftOut.why: Practised inside the narrative and informative writing lessons, which start from what the child remembers.

leftOut.what: SL.K.1.a and SL.K.1.b: rules for discussion and conversation
leftOut.why: Set in the first two weeks of routines and kept every day; the Name Sticks questions and the author's chair practise them.

leftOut.what: SL.K.2 and SL.K.3: ask and answer questions about what is read aloud or said
leftOut.why: Done in every read-aloud and in the story and fact-text question lessons.

leftOut.what: SL.K.4, SL.K.5, SL.K.6: describe, add drawings, speak audibly
leftOut.why: A daily show-and-tell routine; the author's chair lesson carries them.

leftOut.what: L.K.1.d: question words
leftOut.why: Used in the story and fact-text question lessons (who, what, where, why, how) rather than a page of their own.

leftOut.what: L.K.4.b: inflections and affixes as clues
leftOut.why: -s is taught in One and many; -ed, -ing, re- and un- are taught in Grade 1 endings and Grade 2 prefixes, where children can read them.

leftOut.what: L.K.5.c: real-life connections between words and their use
leftOut.why: A daily word-wall talk routine (Where in our school do we see something noisy?), not a page.

leftOut.what: L.K.6: use words acquired through conversations and reading
leftOut.why: The outcome of all vocabulary work, practised daily in talk; not a lesson.

leftOut.what: K:bilingual-cards: bilingual picture word cards
leftOut.why: A word-wall display resource for multilingual classes, not a lesson with a teaching point.
